articleSummary: Hantavirus, an RNA virus from the Hantaviridae family transmitted by rats, threatens Depok, Indonesia, with potential severe pulmonary and renal disease. Transmission mainly occurs through inhalation of dust contaminated with rodent urine, droppings, or saliva; contact with contaminated surfaces and, rarely, rat bites are additional routes. Human-to-human spread is very rare. Children are at heightened risk, especially in environments with dense rodent populations or poor sanitation, such as warehouses, abandoned houses, gardens, or post-flood sites. Cleaning closed or unused spaces without protective equipment increases exposure risk. The warning emphasizes environmental hygiene, rodent population control, and prompt medical evaluation for children suspected of exposure. As of 20 June 2026, FKUI urges vigilance to prevent hantavirus infection.

articleSummary: Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda has surged to 894 confirmed cases with more than 200 deaths as of June 20, 2026. Ituri Province accounts for over 90% of cases; 32 health zones affected. The DRC outbreak's case fatality rate is about 23%. Uganda reports 19 cases and 2 deaths. Nine Ebola treatment centers in Ituri are at over 90% capacity. The outbreak was officially confirmed on May 15 after testing limitations for the Bundibugyo strain delayed recognition. Case growth remains high with a 38% week-over-week increase; contact tracing has traced only about 4,000 of an expected 17,000–35,000 contacts. No approved vaccine or specific treatment exists for Bundibugyo; early aggressive supportive care saves lives. Mass displacement (nearly a million in Ituri), many children malnourished and a large fraction zero-dose, heighten vulnerability and risk of rapid spread, especially in crowded camps like Kpangba (≈30,000).

articleSummary: Petaling Jaya, Malaysia – 16-year-old students from SMK Putrajaya Presint 18 (1) formed Vector Vixens and unveiled Aeroplus at the Asia Dengue Summit on June 17 to curb dengue in dengue-prone communities. articleHeadline: Molecular characterization and whole-genome sequencing-based genetic evolution of coxsackievirus A16 in Taiyuan City, 2023-2025 - Archives of Virology
articleSummary: Coxsackievirus A16 (CVA16), a major cause of hand, foot, and mouth disease (HFMD) in China, was studied in Taiyuan City, Shanxi Province, using 35 CVA16-positive strains from 2023–2025. Genomic analysis shows highest conservation in VP4 and lowest in the 3' UTR. Temporally, CVA16 shifted from B1a/B1b co-circulation to a three-lineage pattern, including a novel B1c subgenotype. Intertypic recombination—primarily at the 5'UTR and VP1/2A junction—drives evolution (B1a with EV71; B1b with CVA4; B1c with both), while the core P1 capsid region remains intact and recombination-free, preserving major antigenic determinants. Positive selection targets four residues (VP1-T97I, VP2-D139T, VP3-I2V, VP3-M126T); these changes moderately reduce capsid stability, suggesting adaptive tuning of assembly kinetics rather than antigenic drift. Three B1b-specific VP1 markers (L23M, I235V, T240A) support temporal adaptation; no significant northern–southern divergence during overlap. Overall, CVA16 evolution is shaped by non-coding recombination and subtle structural refinement, maintaining antigenic relevance for current vaccine candidates.

articleSummary: Ebola virus, Bundibugyo strain, is causing a rapidly expanding outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo, predominantly in Ituri province’s Bunia region, with spread to North Kivu and South Kivu. As of June 20, 2026, WHO-confirmed cases stand at 896 with 232 deaths, including 21 more deaths in the last 24 hours. Emergence was reported on May 15, and the outbreak remains severe and fast-growing, driven by close-contact transmission and exposure to infected body fluids. There is no vaccine or specific treatment for Bundibugyo strain. Healthcare capacity has surged from zero beds to more than 500. Surveillance handles around 400 alerts daily and over 2,000 tests per day; contact tracing has reached about 75% of contacts, with WHO targeting 95%. Some patients delay care, seeking traditional healers before presenting to facilities. By now, 78 have recovered.

articleHeadline: Can Cow Urine Help Fight Chikungunya? IIT Roorkee Study Finds Powerful Antiviral Compounds
articleSummary: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) antiviral activity identified in cow urine distillate (CUD) from IIT Roorkee, India. Laboratory studies show CUD reduces CHIKV viral load by more than 90% at safe concentrations; an optimized formulation combining CUD with thymoquinone (from Nigella sativa) and piperine (black pepper) achieved a 99.85% reduction. Key compounds linked to antiviral efficacy include benzoic acid, hippuric acid, and oleic acid, which appear to inhibit essential replication proteins. The work, conducted by IIT Roorkee's Department of Biosciences and Bioengineering with Ayurveda and biomedicine partners, used virology, metabolomics, molecular docking and biochemical analyses. CHIKV is primarily spread by Aedes mosquitoes and causes fever and joint pain; outbreaks are concentrated in tropical and subtropical regions. The study, funded by the Ministry of AYUSH, calls for further research before therapeutic use, highlighting natural formulations' potential.

articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in northeastern Democratic Republic of Congo shows signs of rapid spread. articleHeadlineTranslated: Study reveals the presence of the Sporotrichosis fungus in wild animals.
articleHeadline: Estudo revela presença de fungo da esporotricose em animais silvestres
articleSummary: Wildlife in Paraná, Brazil harbor Sporothrix DNA, indicating wildlife as a potential reservoir for Sporotrichosis beyond domestic cats. A study published in Mycopathologia and supported by Fapesp detected DNA from Sporothrix brasiliensis (endemic to Brazil), S. globosa, and S. schenckii in internal organs of 81 roadkill animals (heart, liver, lungs, bladder) collected from 2017–2023 along BR-376 and PR-445. S. schenckii was most frequent across mammals, birds, and reptiles. While DNA presence confirms circulation of these fungi in animals, it does not prove active infection. The findings emphasize One Health links between environment, animals, and humans, with higher incidence in ecological transition zones between native habitats and urban areas. Roadkill surveillance is proposed as a low-cost sentinel strategy for zoonotic monitoring, and the study challenges prior assumptions about birds’ role, warranting further histopathological confirmation of active infection.

Histopathology was not performed, but molecular detection indicates fungal circulation, suggesting wildlife as reservoirs with potential human infection through skin lesions and possible lymphatic involvement. Roadkill-based surveillance supports One Health approaches in emerging fungal pathogens.

District vaccination officer Dr. Suchitra Agarwal said Ajmain infections are claimed to have originated from Panna district. The situation is being monitored as the measles outbreak continues in the region.

articleHeadlineTranslated: Natural mosquito trap. Yeast may help reduce malaria.
articleHeadline: Naturalna pułapka na komary. Drożdże mogą pomóc ograniczyć malarię
articleSummary: Orange yeast Rhodotorula taiwanensis can attract and even trap Anopheles gambiae, the malaria vector in Africa. Johns Hopkins Bloomberg School of Public Health researchers found that the odor and stickiness of R. taiwanensis lure both male and female A. gambiae into a sticky biofilm, offering a potential safe, inexpensive malaria-control strategy. R. taiwanensis was first isolated from plant samples in Taiwan and is common in soil and on plants worldwide, including sugarcane and rice leaves, with use in fermentation cultures in India and Korea. Only one of seven tested yeasts showed this attraction: R. taiwanensis 200S, isolated from Anopheles in Baltimore in 2023. The odor mixture is largely acetone and 3-methyl-1-butanol. Related species R. mucilaginosa and R. toruloides were found on Anopheles in a malaria-endemic area in Zambia, indicating natural associations. Malaria kills over 600,000 annually; vector resistance to insecticides and drugs persists; two vaccines are only moderately effective.
notes: 記事サマリーは新規マラリア防除技術（酵母による蚊トラップ）の基礎研究成果の報道。Africaおよび米国Baltimore、韓国は対象国リストに含まれないため除外。インド（発酵文化での使用言及）とザンビア（マラリア流行地での酵母関連種の自然分布報告）のみを対象国として含める。実際の感染症イベント（患者発生、流行）ではなく、技術開発段階のため、WATCH判定。

articleHeadline: RD Kongo laporkan 956 kasus terkonfirmasi ebola, 247 kematian
articleSummary: In the Democratic Republic of Congo, Ebola (Bundibugyo ebolavirus) totals reached 956 confirmed cases and 247 deaths as of the June 20, 2026 situation report. Ituri Province and North Kivu reported 23 newly confirmed cases on June 19, including two deaths; Ituri remains the epicenter with 874 confirmed cases and 201 deaths, accounting for over 91% of the national total. So far 92 patients have recovered, and 361 are in isolation or hospitalized. There were 162 suspected cases identified that day, and contact tracing efficiency stood at 69.3% against a 95% target. Health Minister Roger Kamba said the outbreak is in an expansion phase, with more cases expected as responders broaden active-case finding and deepen community engagement. The Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak was declared in Congo on May 15, 2026.

articleSummary: Shigella infections are rising in Kerala, India, with over 200 people affected and five deaths reported this year; as of 21 June 2026, 133 cases are active and five have died. On Saturday, 13 new cases were identified across Kozhikode (4), Malappuram (3), Kannur (3), Palakkad (2), and Kollam (1). June shows the highest activity in Kozhikode and Wayanad. Transmission is primarily through contaminated food or water, amplified during the monsoon, with person-to-person spread possible. Symptoms include diarrhea, abdominal pain, fever, dehydration, and sometimes mucus or blood in stool. The elderly and children under five are at higher risk; severe illness requires urgent hospitalization. In Kozhikode, a Nipah virus patient remains ventilated; 15 Nipah-exposed contacts with symptoms tested negative.
notes: 記事はシゲラ菌の流行を主題としているが、ケララ州ではニパウイルス患者（人工呼吸中）の報告も記載されている。水系感染とモンスーン時期の関連が指摘されており、公衆衛生上の懸念が高い。複数地区に拡大している点が重要。
